Krichene and Rendle’s [On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) (KDD 2020) shows that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation—even in expectation. Repeating candidate draws estimates sampling variability but cannot remove this bias. Smaller candidate sets also make distinct ranking metrics increasingly resemble AUC. [Candidate Set Sampling for Evaluating Top-N Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11723) specifically studies how candidate selection interacts with popularity bias; changing the negative distribution changes the evaluation problem.

Suggested diagnostic design, inferred from these findings: compare uniform negatives, popularity-matched negatives, and content-similar negatives matched to the same popularity distribution. Define popularity using training interactions only; derive lexical similarity from available titles/descriptions. The content-similar versus popularity-matched contrast better isolates lexical competition, although it remains observational. Hold candidate count, positive target, history exclusions, and unique-item requirements constant. Use the same eligible queries across conditions, but report eligibility coverage and excluded-query characteristics: restricting to queries with enough content-similar candidates changes the population and can introduce selection bias.

Repeat auxiliary candidate draws with prespecified seeds, pairing queries and draws across model comparisons. Report paired differences, uncertainty across draws, and user-level bootstrap intervals separately; candidate repetitions are not additional independent users. Krichene and Rendle’s [extended abstract](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651) explicitly discusses sampling variance and bias–variance trade-offs. Keep these analyses diagnostic: retain the pinned host’s 99-negative, seed-42 macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion, without replacing it with corrected metrics or alternative candidate distributions.
